claims.text: Elevated temperatures promote short-range order among Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr atoms.
Elevated temperatures promote nanoscale clustering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range order and nanoscale clustering alter interatomic bonding.
Short-range order and nanoscale clustering alter dislocation mobility.
Changes in bonding and dislocation mobility produce anomalous work hardening at elevated temperature.
Changes associated with short-range order and clustering produce nonlinear thermal expansion relative to the as-cast state.
The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy has a random atomic distribution.
Annealing at 700–900°C and pre-straining can be used to promote or suppress short-range order.
At elevated temperatures, atomic diffusion facilitates local rearrangements that form or modify short-range order.
The resulting clusters enhance interatomic bonding.
The resulting clusters impede dislocation mobility.
Annealed and pre-strained specimens will have higher yield and flow stresses than the as-cast alloy at elevated temperatures.
Annealed and pre-strained specimens will exhibit a noticeable elevated-temperature work-hardening plateau.
Annealed and pre-strained specimens will exhibit nonlinear thermal expansion or reduced thermal-expansion coefficients relative to the as-cast alloy.
Annealing and pre-straining will produce distinct lattice-parameter changes accompanied by detectable short-range order or clustering.
The as-cast alloy exhibits conventional linear thermal expansion.
The as-cast alloy exhibits a continuous decrease in yield strength as temperature rises.
The proposed mechanism should govern behavior from approximately 300°C to 1200°C under controlled mechanical loading.
Outside the proposed temperature range, grain growth or phase precipitation may dominate the responses.
